replacement: “What, am I to stay naked?” he shouted.
“So am I to stay naked like this?” he added savagely.
“Damn his sorrow! Well, where to now? Do I just go on sitting here?”
“But you told us yourself that the envelope was under your late father’s pillow. You specifically said it was under the pillow, so you must have known.”
Mitya was indescribably agitated. He went pale.

“Why were you so reticent? Why did you make such a secret of it? To put it more exactly: you have now told us your secret, which you yourself call ‘disgraceful.’ Yet in reality—comparatively speaking, of course—this act, the taking of three thousand roubles belonging to someone else, and only for a time, naturally, is in my view merely extreme recklessness, and not so disgraceful, given your character.... Grant that it was highly discreditable. Still, discreditable is not ‘disgraceful.’... Many people have guessed during this last month that you spent Katerina Ivanovna’s three thousand, and I heard the tale myself, quite apart from your confession.... Mihail Makarovitch, for one, had heard it as well, so that it was hardly a tale any more, just the gossip of the whole town. There are also signs, if I am not mistaken, that you admitted this yourself to somebody, I mean that the money was Katerina Ivanovna’s. So I am greatly surprised that up to this moment you have made such an extraordinary secret of the fifteen hundred you say you set aside, and have, apparently, attached a feeling of positive horror to that secret.... It is hard to believe that confessing it could cost you such anguish.... Just now you cried out that Siberia would be better than confessing it ...”

“Yes, I see a vital difference! Any man can be a scoundrel, and perhaps every man is one, but not everyone can be a thief. For that you have to be an arch-scoundrel. Oh, of course, I don’t know how to draw these fine lines ... but a thief is lower than a scoundrel, that’s what I believe. Listen: I carry the money on me for a whole month. Any day I might make up my mind to give it back, and then I’m not a scoundrel anymore. But I can’t make up my mind, you see, though I decide every day, every day I push myself to do it, and still for a whole month I can’t bring myself to it. Is that right, do you think? Is that right?”
